official_sources_checked: St Helena eVisa FAQ — https://evisa.sainthelena.gov.sh/faq; SHG Immigration Policy (13 June 2024) — https://www.sainthelena.gov.sh/documents/Final-Immigration-Policy-240613.pdf; Short Term Entry Permit — https://www.sainthelena.gov.sh/st-helena/government/portfolios/safety-security-and-home-affairs/immigration/short-term-entry-permit/; Immigration Amendment Ordinance 2026 announcement — https://www.sainthelena.gov.sh/shg-announces-approval-of-immigration-amendment-ordinance-2026/; eVisa application page — https://evisa.sainthelena.gov.sh/apply/
exact_blocker: The current official eVisa FAQ says there is no cost for an eVisa application, while the official SHG Immigration Policy (13 June 2024) lists a £50 standard fee for visa nationals or £100 expedited fee. The current Short Term Entry Permit page separately lists a £20 entry fee. The policy and eVisa FAQ do not explain whether the £20 entry fee is additional to the visa-national application fee or whether the 2024 fee table has been superseded. The 2026 Immigration (Amendment) Ordinance was approved on 3 August 2026 but the Government says it will commence only on a date fixed by the Governor; no commencement order was located in the official Gazette during this check. The current eVisa application page still limits eVisa to 183 days.
next_research_action: Request written confirmation from St Helena Immigration Service of the current fee payable by Bangladesh visa-required eVisa applicants, whether the £20 short-term entry-permit fee is additional, and whether a commencement order has brought the 2026 holiday-permit amendment into force. Then rerun the nationality-specific eVisa check.

exact_blocker: Bangladesh is absent from the official visa-exempt nationality list and therefore requires a visitor visa unless a qualifying UK/US/Canada visa or residence status exemption is granted. However, the current visitor-visa service page and its linked 2016 Rev.2 application form conflict: the web page asks for the applicant's original bank reference, while the form asks for the surety's bank reference; the form also includes proof of vaccination for applicants over 12, which the current web checklist omits. The fee page uses '$' without a currency code, and does not state processing time or permitted stay. The receiving mission for Bangladesh is not identified.
next_research_action: Obtain written confirmation from TCI Border Force or the Director of Immigration of the current bank-reference requirement, whether vaccination proof remains mandatory, the fee currency, permitted stay, processing estimate, and which mission accepts applications from Bangladesh. Publish only after the current checklist is reconciled.
